name: PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk

frontmatter.title: Chandra Asri: a doubled buyback, a smaller subsidiary mark and a target cut that is mostly the lens
frontmatter.summary: Chandra Asri doubled its buyback and the shares fell again. The buyback is value-neutral: treasury stock, no cash out, count held flat. We re-mark the forty per cent CDIA minority at CDIA's own fundamental today and fix the cost, working-capital and liquid-asset assumptions. Most of the target cut is the price-driven lens, not the subsidiary. ADD at Rp1,610.
thesis: The enlarged platform is real: FY2025 revenue reached US$7,000.0m and H1-2026 revenue US$5,348.8m after the Aster refinery and Esso retail acquisitions, with management reporting record operating EBITDA of US$802.6m for the half [S5, S2, S6].

Reported FY2025 profit is not operating profit: it contains a US$1,772.2m pre-tax bargain-purchase gain on Aster, larger than the full-year attributable profit, so the headline and the LTM multiples built on it are unusable [S2, S6].

The balance sheet carries the expansion: finance costs of US$187.9m in the half and FY2026E net debt of US$3,210.0m at 2.5x EBITDA, with a current debt wall of about three-quarters of a billion dollars against US$2,921.3m of cash [S2].
The new buyback is verified at up to IDR2.00tn, 1,600m shares (1.84%), at Rp3,000 to 28 January 2027; the shares go to treasury, so it is value-neutral and we hold the count flat [S13, S14, S12].

The CDIA minority is marked at the CDIA coverage model's own probability-weighted fundamental today, not its premium-bearing target; the through-cycle DCF is Rp1,408 and the konglo-lens target Rp1,610, a 20.0% return at Rp1,350 [S0, F42].

catalysts.event: Nine-month 2026 results and any update on the CA-EDC Phase II plan
End of the buyback period; executed volume and the treasury balance
CA-EDC chlor-alkali and EDC plant scheduled start-up
MSCI consultation feedback closes; decision on Standalone status due mid-2027

blocks.text: What changed. The buyback headline is half right: the new programme runs from 29 October 2026 to 28 January 2027, and the 28 October date is the termination of the old one [S12, S13, S14]. The forty per cent CDIA minority is re-marked to CDIA's own probability-weighted fundamental today, with the book value from the filing [S2, S15]. Three red-team inputs are corrected: the operating-cost ratio, the working-capital ratio and the liquid-portfolio haircut [S2]. We stay at ADD with a target of Rp1,610 against Rp1,350, a 20.0% return; the twelve-month fundamental is Rp1,767 [S0].

The target walk, exactly. The published note carried a fundamental value near two thousand rupiah and a premium-kept ratio of about nine-tenths at a fifteen-hundred price. The draft, at the thirteen-hundred-and-fifty price, cut the target by about one hundred and thirty-nine rupiah. The larger part is the lens, not the CDIA re-mark: the fall in the premium-kept ratio to about seven-eighths accounts for about eighty-two rupiah, three-fifths of the cut, while the change in the fundamental value, multiplied by the prior ratio, accounts for the other roughly fifty-seven, and the CDIA re-mark sits inside that fundamental term [S0, S15]. This revision then applies the three input fixes, taking the fundamental to Rp1,767 and the target to Rp1,610. That last step is not the fundamental move applied whole: the premium-kept ratio rises from about seven-eighths to about nine-tenths as the fundamental falls toward the price, so of the roughly thirty-seven rupiah the target gives up, about a hundred and seventeen comes from the fundamental and about eighty is added back by the lens [S0].

The buyback is value-neutral. The company terminated its earlier programme at the close of the second session on 28 October 2026; it had run from 19 October with IDR1.00tn and a cap of 800m shares [S12, S7]. The replacement is up to IDR2.00tn, 1,600m shares or 1.84% of the count, at a maximum of Rp3,000 [S13, S14]. The shares are treasury stock and the engine carries no cash-out line; shrinking the count without its cash cost would overstate equity value, so we hold the count flat and the programme does not move our value or target [S13, S14, S0]. At the market price it is near neutral against our fundamental value; at the ceiling it would destroy value, so the ceiling is support intent, not worth.

The platform and the variant view. Aster, the former Shell park bought with Glencore, and the Esso retail network turned a domestic cracker into an integrated refinery and petrochemical group [S4, S5]. FY2025 net profit of US$1,090.1m flatters earning power because H1-2025 carries a US$1,772.2m bargain-purchase gain larger than the full-year attributable profit; strip it out and pack EBITDA was US$-389.2m, while H1-2026 operating EBITDA of US$802.6m is the first clean read [S2, S0, S6].

What moves the value is the spread first, then Brent — only four-fifths of a feedstock move passes into prices — then the balance sheet, where FY2026E net debt of US$3,210.0m at 2.5x EBITDA deleverages as CA-EDC starts [S2, S5, S0].

Chandra Asri Pacific is the listed chemicals and energy arm of the Barito Pacific group, controlled by Prajogo Pangestu, with plants in Banten [S2]. It reports three pillars, and the infrastructure one is the separately listed PT Chandra Daya Investasi, 60 per cent owned [S5, S2].

Chemicals is the original naphtha cracker and polyolefins business. Aster adds refinery products and petrochemicals and is why revenue multiplied; Aster Polymer Solutions adds 400 ktpa of HDPE capacity [S4, S5]. CDIA runs power, water, port, storage and logistics, and we value the consolidated group net of its forty per cent minority [S5, S2, F42]. The growth story is CA-EDC, a US$800.0m chlor-alkali and EDC project more than half complete and scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, with Danantara and INA co-investing [S5]. A second phase is excluded from capex until a final investment decision [S6].
A naphtha cracker is a price-taker on both sides: feedstock is priced off oil and polymers off regional supply, so the operator's advantage is reliability, scale and downstream integration.

Asian petrochemicals are in a supply-driven downcycle. Management calls the market still challenging: Chinese and Middle Eastern capacity has pushed spreads toward cash cost and older Japanese and Korean crackers are closing [S6]. The marginal producer's cash cost anchors the price, so we value on a through-cycle spread and treat the oil tape as a timing input [S0].

The cost curve runs through oil. The house oil deck has Brent at 96 for FY2026E, 84 for FY2027E and a long-run anchor of 75, against a FY2025 average of 68; spot is 112. The path raises feedstock cost and, with partial pass-through, squeezes the spread before oil reverts. The sign is not one-way: H1-2026, earned at a higher Brent than FY2025, had a materially better gross margin because cracks widened with the feedstock move [S2]. We carry only the cost side, so the oil spike does not lift the through-cycle value.

Competitive position rests on integration and scale, not cost leadership: the refinery gives feedstock flexibility and the cracker local access, but neither is durable against a Middle East gas-based producer. We place the complex mid-curve, not first quartile; the LK carries no cost-curve data, so that is our judgment [S2]. Five forces read badly on commodity polymers — high supplier and buyer power, high rivalry — and better in EDC and caustic, where the domestic alternative is an import [S5]. Market share is not disclosed in a comparable series [S2].

FY2022 to FY2024 show the domestic business in a trough, revenue down to US$1,785.4m and gross profit barely positive [S0]. FY2025 is the transformation year, revenue US$7,000.0m with Aster consolidated from mid-year, but EBITDA US$-389.2m because the refinery ran at trough spreads and the enlarged base carries full-year depreciation [S0]. Those FY2025 lines are pack- and management-derived; the audited consolidated statements are not yet archived, so we mark the last actual unverified and carry the archive to the next refresh [S0, S5].

H1-2026 is the first clean half. Revenue was US$5,348.8m, raw materials and manufacturing US$4,455.5m, leaving a gross margin of sixteen point seven per cent; depreciation of US$164.1m sits below gross profit and finance costs were US$187.9m [S2]. Management reports operating EBITDA of US$802.6m and net profit of US$283.2m attributable to shareholders [S6, S2].

Our forecast. FY2026E revenue grows 52.0% to US$10,640.0m on a full year of Aster and the first year of Esso retail, then three per cent as CA-EDC starts [S5]. The 19.1% gross margin is the base-input margin at the FY2025 Brent anchor, not the clean-half run-rate; repricing it through the oil link gives 15.1% in FY2026E and 16.8% in FY2027E as Brent falls, and "holding the spread" in section five means holding that base-input margin [S2, S0]. At the deck's long-run Brent the link lands the effective terminal margin near eighteen per cent, so the DCF never runs at the reference margin itself [S0]. The gap to the clean half is the deck's Brent of 96 against the mid-eighties of H1-2026 and the four-fifths pass-through: at the clean-half margin held at the deck's Brent the DCF would be about four-tenths higher and the twelve-month fundamental about a third higher, which is bull-case territory [S2, S0].

Costs. The opex ratio is now the full H1-2026 reconciliation: selling US$41.6m, G&A US$91.3m, final tax US$3.3m, other net loss US$39.1m and depreciation US$164.1m sum to 6.3% of revenue. The prior ratio omitted part of the other net loss; we keep the loss recurring because the note does not call it one-off, a disclosed conservatism [S2]. The Brent link is a calibration: sixty per cent of the cost base is oil-linked and four-fifths passes into prices, a net twelve per cent exposure that reproduces the clean half [S2].

Cash flow and capex. H1-2026 PP&E acquisitions were US$283.8m, and we forecast capex at five and a half per cent of revenue while CA-EDC completes, stepping to four per cent [S2, S6]. Working capital is calibrated to the last actual, with receivables plus inventories less payables about thirteen per cent of annualised H1-2026 revenue, and we hold that ratio rather than assume an unsourced normalisation, so FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is US$-272.4m [S2]. At the prior ten per cent ratio the first-year FCFF would be positive, the red-team artefact [S2, S0].

Balance sheet and debt. The forecast rolls from the 30 June 2026 LK, with opening cash US$2,739.8m and opening debt after the half-year drawdown at US$5,910.9m [S2]. FY2026E net debt is US$3,210.0m at 2.5x EBITDA, deleveraging to US$2,293.5m by FY2028E [S0]. Within a year sit short-term bank loans of US$399.2m, lease maturities of US$75.3m, current bank installments of US$180.2m and current bonds of US$113.7m — about three-quarters of a billion dollars — against cash of US$2,921.3m; the long-term stack is US$4,198.7m of bank and US$575.4m of bonds [S2]. Base interest cover is a little over three and a half times; the bear takes cover to about two and a half times and net debt to about four times EBITDA, the covenant test that matters [S0].

Capital allocation and quality. The company pays a small dividend, US$30.0m at the parent in H1-2026, and buys back stock opportunistically [S2, S0]. The verified position is the IDR2.00tn programme to January 2027 for 1,600m shares at Rp3,000; the shares are treasury stock and execution is discretionary, so the count is flat [S13, S14, S12]. The bargain-purchase gain of US$1,772.2m is non-recurring and excluded; the working-capital build is a scope effect but a real cash cost; and FY2025 total profit of US$1,400.0m is not the attributable US$1,090.1m because minorities are material [S2].

We value TPIA on a through-cycle FCFF DCF, with forward EV/EBITDA and PE cross-checks at the peer median. The industry map defaults to sixty per cent DCF, a quarter EV/EBITDA and fifteen per cent PE; we weight the DCF fully because the engine computes the multiple legs only on trailing pack metrics, where FY2025A EBITDA of US$-389.2m is negative and parent earnings of US$1,090.1m contain the US$1,772.2m bargain-purchase gain [S0, S2]. A negative EV leg floors to zero, a gain-inflated PE leg capitalises an item we exclude, and the card forbids current-year multiples [S0]. The forward multiples are a cycle-position sensitivity, not a value, which is why the table carries one weighted method [S0].

The cost of capital is a risk-free rate of 5.0%, an equity risk premium plus country risk of 4.2% and 2.5%, an unlevered beta of 0.90 levered to 1.54, and a pre-tax cost of debt of 7.0%, giving a cost of equity of 15.3% and a WACC of 10.6% [S0]. The cost of debt is the normalised forward build, not the LK's trailing cash cost for older fixed-rate facilities [S2].

The DCF produces Rp1,408 a share, with terminal value 49.5% of the total [S0]. The CDIA mark. The method card's SOTP default marks a covered listed subsidiary at its house target, because the target already carries that subsidiary's own konglo lens. This is not a SOTP case: TPIA consolidates CDIA and deducts a forty per cent non-controlling interest, so the mark is a minority-deduction basis and must be struck on the same basis as the consolidated cash flow, and the earlier red team required CDIA's premium to be kept out of TPIA's fundamental value. We therefore mark the minority at CDIA's own probability-weighted fundamental today, which gives the Rp1,610 target and 20.0% return we carry; the CDIA coverage model marks today's fundamental at a hundred and nineteen point five rupiah, a twelve-month fundamental at a hundred and thirty, and a target at two hundred and eighty-seven, against a market price near three hundred and sixty-two, the share count in the CDIA filing [S15, F42, F43]. A higher mark applied one-for-one would overstate the downside: the parent's premium-kept ratio rises as the fundamental falls toward the price: at the twelve-month mark the parent DCF is about six rupiah lower and the lens target about two lower, a return of about a fifth; at the target the DCF is about ninety-six lower but premium kept rises from about nine-tenths to about ninety-five per cent, so the lens target falls only about thirty-one, to fifteen hundred and seventy-nine and a return of seventeen point six per cent. ADD holds across the range [S0, F42].

Cycle position and the oil NAV. Spot Brent is 112 against a long-run anchor of 75 [S0]. Held at the anchor through the forecast, the DCF is about five per cent higher than base because the deck's near-term path is above it; held at spot with no mean reversion it collapses to about a tenth and the lens target would sit below the price, a reduce. The crack-offset case sits between: the clean-half margin at the deck's Brent lifts the DCF by about four-tenths because the model carries only the cost side of oil [S2, S0].

The cross-checks, reconciled. The shares trade at 8.5x FY2026E and 6.9x FY2027E EV/EBITDA, and at 14.1x and 11.4x PE [S0]. At the peer median the FY2026E and FY2027E values sit about a third and a sixth below the DCF, and the PE about a third below; the DCF's enterprise value implies a little over six and a half times FY2027E EBITDA, about an eighth above the median. The gap is cycle and perimeter: a trailing multiple on smaller domestic names against a DCF that capitalises the through-cycle recovery and CA-EDC, and a trough multiple would value the trough, which the card forbids. The PE check is weakest, on a small peer set and the enlarged depreciation base [S0].

Two points of gross margin either side moves the twelve-month value between roughly two-thirds and four-thirds of the base; a one-point WACC change moves it less [S0]. No public Asian petrochemical spread index exists in our archive, so the marker is the clean-half margin paired with the FY2022 to FY2025 history, and the quartile is a judgment [S2, S0].

What the price implies. A reverse DCF says the Rp1,350 price discounts long-run revenue growth of 2.5%, below the 3.0% we forecast, so the margin of safety is in the spread, not the growth assumption [S0].

The konglo lens. Price is 0.88 times our fundamental value today of Rp1,540.4 — a discount — and below the twelve-month fundamental of Rp1,767 [S0]. The lens assumes only part of the gap closes: the base regime case closes 30.0% of the log gap and the bull 70.0%, so the target is Rp1,610, below the twelve-month fundamental and above the price [S0]. The float is thin, the stock has been deleted from the MSCI Global Standard index, and the marginal buyer is a flow investor [S11, S8].

The business scenarios are mirrored: the bear cuts revenue growth four points and the gross margin three, the bull adds the same [S0]. The base carries half the probability and holds the base-input margin in real terms, not the clean-half run-rate, giving the effective path from 15.1% to 16.8% [S0]. The payoff is convex — the bull is about double the base twelve-month value and the bear about a third of it — so the probability-weighted value sits about a tenth above the base and the lens discount lands the target on the base value [S0]. The regime cases map the premium or discount separately — the base closes 30.0% of the gap, the bear widens it — which is why the target sits between price and fundamental [S0].

Regulatory and index risk, high likelihood, medium impact. The OJK has raised the minimum free float to fifteen per cent with a first deadline in March 2027, and MSCI has frozen index increases and opened a Standalone consultation, with feedback to April 2027 and a decision by mid-year [S8, S9]. A further deletion would remove flow buyers from a thin register [S11].

Commodity and spread risk, high likelihood, high impact. Renewed Chinese capacity would compress the spread; this is the dominant sensitivity and why the bear is a spread case, not a volume case [S0].

Macro and FX risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. Revenue is dollar-denominated and the shares rupiah-denominated; the macro desk has the rupiah under balance-of-payments pressure and its tilt for oil-import beneficiaries is AVOID, which we carry as a headwind [S0]. A weaker rupiah raises the rupiah value of a dollar DCF but also imported input costs [S0].
Operational risk, medium likelihood, high impact. A cracker or refinery outage at the site is an earnings event [S5].

Liquidity and balance-sheet risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. Heavy debt against cyclical EBITDA and a thin float make refinancing a flow event as much as a credit event [S2]. The liquid portfolio is a real cushion, but it is carried in the bridge at full fair value and is therefore already inside equity value; it is not counted twice [S2, S0]. It is bonds, listed shares, money-market and credit-linked investments, all performing with a low-credit-risk twelve-month ECL and no encumbrance disclosed; the prior ten per cent haircut was unsourced and is removed, worth about eleven rupiah a share [S2]. The risk is trough timing — a CA-EDC delay or a second downcycle at this debt level — not immediate solvency [S0, S2].

Governance and group risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. The controller owns most of the company and the group has multiple listed vehicles, so the risk is that value moves between group vehicles rather than being earned in TPIA [S2]. On pledges, the interim LK cannot show controlling-share pledges, so we flag a gap rather than a clean bill [S2].

Signposts. A sustained spread recovery, an on-time CA-EDC start and index eligibility restored by a higher float would push us more constructive; a renewed oversupply wave or a Standalone decision would push the other way [S0, S9].

Commodity chemical equities usually bottom when the marginal producer is losing cash and capacity is closing, not when headline profit recovers. That timing mismatch is why the card insists on a through-cycle value.

Ownership and control. TPIA belongs to the Barito Pacific group of Prajogo Pangestu [S2]. The registry puts insider ownership at seventy-four per cent and the free float at 25.4%, above the fifteen per cent minimum but concentrated enough that the controller sets the agenda [S0, S8]. The register is concentrated, so the price can sit away from fundamental value longer than the business cycle, which is why the lens assumes only part of today's discount closes [S2, S0].

The 2026 regime. The OJK rule raises the minimum free float from seven and a half to fifteen per cent, with a March 2027 first deadline and a delisting path [S8]. MSCI froze index increases, deletes names under the HSC framework, and opened the Standalone consultation on 15 October 2026 [S9]. TPIA was deleted from the Global Standard index at the May 2026 review, but it is not on the exchange's HSC list in the latest publication, so the deletion is an index-flow event, not a finding of wrongdoing [S11, S10]. The March 2027 deadline does not bind TPIA: its float of 25.4% clears the minimum and the interim step, so it is a market-wide regime date and, if anything, a relative positive against less-compliant peers [S8, S0].

Group transactions. Aster was acquired with Glencore, and Sembcorp Utilities has announced a planned acquisition of twenty per cent of Aster Power; the H1-2026 profit correction is explained by that planned transaction, not a completed sale [S6]. Related-party trade is small: sales 1.9% of revenue, raw-material purchases 0.05% and finished-goods purchases 0.06% [S2]. Auditor, dividend, ESG. The interim accounts are unaudited, and the LK presents depreciation below gross profit, hence our opex treatment [S2]; we have not sourced the latest auditor's opinion and flag that gap. ESG exposures are carbon intensity, process safety at a large integrated site, and water and waste around the Cilegon estate; sustainability awards are not evidence of lower risk [S5].

The nine-month results and any CA-EDC Phase II update are the next hard operating data [S6]. The buyback ends on 28 January 2027; executed volume against the Rp3,000 ceiling and IDR2.00tn fund tells us whether it is a bid or an authorisation [S13, S14]. CA-EDC start-up in the first quarter of 2027 validates the growth case [S5]. The MSCI consultation closes at the end of April 2027 and the decision follows by end-June; it is the largest regime catalyst [S9]. The March 2027 free-float deadline is market-wide and does not bind TPIA [S8].

Between updates we watch five KPIs, each tied to the model [S6, S2]: gross margin, our spread proxy and main DCF driver; operating EBITDA on the LK-consistent definition; operating cash flow over EBITDA, where working capital is the quality question; net debt and interest cover; and the free float against index news, because flows set the marginal price [S0, S8]. A placement or asset injection would change the count, flat today because the buyback is treasury-bound [S2, S13, S14].

bear.narrative: Chinese and Middle East capacity keeps polymer spreads compressed while a high Brent deck lifts naphtha with only partial pass-through; the refinery runs at mid-cycle, CA-EDC start-up slips, and the enlarged debt load keeps interest cover thin.

bull.narrative: Petrochemical spreads widen as older Asian crackers shut, the Singapore refinery captures a strong diesel and jet margin, CA-EDC starts on time into a protected domestic caustic and EDC market, and the balance sheet deleverages faster than assumed.

groups.name: Barito group (Prajogo Pangestu)
groups.role: petrochemicals, refining and infrastructure; parent of CDIA (60%)

index_deletions.note: deleted at the May 2026 review; AMRT moved to Small Cap

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +52% is the first full year of Aster Chemicals and Energy (ex-Shell Singapore refinery, acquired with Glencore) plus the Esso retail network from 1 Jan 2026, which took FY2025 revenue to about US$7.0bn against H1-2026 revenue of US$5.35bn [S5, S2]; afterwards +3% a year from CA-EDC start-up in Q1 2027 and volume growth, not price [S5].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Through-cycle marker, not a spot number: H1-2026 gross margin of 16.7% (revenue US$5.35bn less raw materials and manufacturing US$4.46bn) was earned with Brent near US$85, above the FY2025 anchor of US$68.1 [S2]. Grossing it back through the calibrated oil link gives a 19.1% margin at base input costs; the gross-up is our calibration, not a disclosed figure, because FY2025 itself is a transition year with Aster consolidated only mid-year [S2, S0]. No public Asian petrochemical spread index exists in our archive, so the clean-half margin paired with the FY2022-25 pack history (gross profit barely positive in the best trough year) is the marker we use; the cost-curve quartile is a judgment, not a disclosure, and we place the group mid-curve because its naphtha cracker and Singapore refinery compete against Middle East gas-based units, not because of a published quartile [S2, S0]. Held flat in real terms, no spread expansion assumed; the report shows value at plus or minus two points of spread.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: we set 60% of COGS as oil-linked because naphtha and refinery crude dominate raw materials while utilities, labour and fixed manufacturing cost do not move with Brent [S2]. The pair split/pass is fitted on the only clean consolidated half, H1-2026, and tested against the FY2025 and H1-2025 comparatives below, which are scope-broken because Aster consolidated only from mid-2025 [S2].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: with the 60% cost share, 80% pass-through gives a net 12% of COGS exposed to the Brent move, which is the pair that reproduces the 16.7% H1-2026 gross margin at that half's Brent and the 19.1% base margin at the FY2025 anchor [S2]. The H1-2026 half is the only clean scope; FY2025 and H1-2025 margins are distorted by the mid-2025 Aster consolidation and therefore cannot validate the pair [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Full reconciliation to the H1-2026 LK lines: selling 41.554 + G&A 91.346 + final tax 3.286 + other net loss 39.101 + depreciation 164.131 = US$339.418m on revenue of US$5,348.769m, which is 6.35% [S2]. The prior 6.2% omitted part of the other net loss; the ratio is restated to the full build. Depreciation sits below the gross-profit line in this LK, so it is included here and added back to EBITDA. The other net loss is kept as recurring because the note does not identify it as one-off; excluding it would lower the ratio to 5.6% and raise value, so it is a disclosed conservatism, not a hidden one [S2].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 depreciation of US$164.1m on US$5,348.8m revenue (3.07%); the pack's FY2025 D&A is close to the LK run-rate, so no restatement is needed [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 acquisitions of PP&E were US$283.8m (5.3% of revenue), running the US$800m CA-EDC project and sustaining the refinery and cracker; it steps down to 4% once CA-EDC completes in Q1 2027, converging on D&A plus growth [S2, S5]. CA-EDC Phase II, which management says is at the preparation stage at a similar size, is disclosed but excluded from the capex path until a final investment decision; including it would add capex without adding the revenue it is meant to earn, so the base carries Phase I only and the report flags the omission [S6].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Calibrated to the last actual: trade receivables US$844m plus inventories US$2,238m less trade and other payables US$1,710m equals US$1,372m, 12.8% of annualised H1-2026 revenue of US$10,698m [S2]. The 8% FY2025 ratio predates a full year of Esso retail inventory and is not comparable. We hold 12.8% flat because no archived source supports a normalisation pace; any release as the Esso inventory settles is upside we do not put in the base [S2].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 income tax of US$62.8m on PBT of US$434.0m is 14.5%, reflecting final tax and incentives; we start at the observed 14.5% and step toward the 22% statutory rate by FY2029E as the mix normalises [S2].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 finance costs of US$187.9m annualise to US$375.7m against US$5.91bn of debt at 30 Jun 2026, a 6.4% average cash cost including the refinery acquisition facilities [S2].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the LK's cash and cash equivalents: H1-2026 finance income of US$60.8m annualises to US$121.7m on the LK cash of US$2,921.3m, a 4.2% yield; on the opening LK cash of US$2,739.8m this gives FY2026E interest income close to the earlier figure, so net income barely moves [S2].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E only: the LK's financing-liabilities reconciliation shows the total rising from US$5,414.2m at 1 January 2026 to US$5,910.9m at 30 June 2026, so the forecast is rolled from the balance-sheet-date debt of US$5,910.9m; the US$496.7m is the H1 drawdown already in the 30 Jun 2026 LK. Thereafter no new net debt: operating EBITDA and capex broadly fund interest and the small dividend [S2, S6, S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the US$1.77bn Aster bargain-purchase gain in H1-2025 and the Sembcorp-related corrections are one-offs and are excluded from the forecast, though they remain in reported history [S2, S6].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 profit attributable to non-controlling interests was US$87.9m of US$371.2m (24%), driven by the 40% CDIA minority and the Glencore/Sembcorp interests in the Aster complex [S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The group paid US$30m of parent dividends in H1-2026 and US$50m in FY2025; the 10% payout reflects the modest DPS on the enlarged share count rather than a stated policy ratio [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Held flat. The new programme, disclosed on 29 October 2026, runs to 28 January 2027 for up to Rp2tn, 1.6bn shares (1.84% of issued) at a maximum of Rp3,000 a share, after the 19 October programme (Rp1tn, up to 0.92%) was terminated on 28 October 2026 [S13, S14, S12]. We still do not shrink the count: the shares are bought into treasury (an asset, not a cancelled share), execution is discretionary and undisclosed to date, and the engine carries no buyback cash-out line, so a count cut without its cash cost would overstate equity value; at the market price the repurchase is close to value-neutral against our fundamental value, while the Rp3,000 ceiling sits well above it, which we read as group intent to support the price rather than as a valuation input [S14, S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: US-dollar reporting: 2.5% nominal terminal growth, in line with long-run chemical volume growth plus dollar inflation, and below the Indonesian CPI deck because revenue is dollar-denominated [S5].

challenges.challenge: The update attributes its target cut to the CDIA re-mark, but the arithmetic says the largest part is the price-driven konglo lens, and the buyback is value-neutral. Published v1: fundamental 1,965.00 x premium kept 0.90863 = 1,785.47. v2: 1,902.37 x 0.865482 = 1,646.47. Decomposition: (1,902.37 - 1,965.00) x 0.90863 = -Rp56.9 from the fundamental/CDIA change, and 1,902.37 x (0.865482 - 0.90863) = -Rp82.1 from premium kept falling as the price went from 1,500 to 1,350; the lens term is 59% of the -Rp139 cut. The summary also says "Both changes are reflected in a lower value and target" although section 4 says "the buyback does not change our value" (share_change 0, no cash-out line). Required: a v1-to-v2 target bridge and a plain statement that the buyback is value-neutral and does not lower the target.
challenges.answer: The v1-to-v2 walk is now stated exactly at the top of the Investment summary: of the Rp139 cut, about Rp82 (59%) is the price-driven lens, premium kept 0.90863 to 0.865482 as the price fell 1,500 to 1,350, and about Rp57 is the fundamental change that contains the CDIA re-mark (1,965.00 x 0.90863 = 1,785.47; 1,902.37 x 0.865482 = 1,646.47). The report then adds a third step for this revision's three input fixes, so the target of Rp1,610 is not conflated with the earlier walk. The buyback is stated as value-neutral in the summary, section 3 and section 6: treasury stock, no cash-out line, count held flat, and the ceiling is support intent, not value.

challenges.challenge: The house standard is a primary method plus two cross-checks (cov_report lint warns "only 1 valuation methods available"), and the 100% DCF is not reconciled to the forward multiples the report itself prints. The shares trade at 8.10x FY2026E and 6.54x FY2027E EV/EBITDA against a peer median of 5.937x (n=14) that is never stated. At 5.937x, FY2027E EBITDA of 1,501.8 gives about Rp1,194/share and FY2026E EBITDA of 1,276.1 about Rp913, 21-40% below the DCF's 1,518; the 8.147x peer-median PE on FY2027E parent earnings of 583.2 gives about Rp996. The DCF's own EV implies 6.97x FY2027E, a 17% premium to the peer median. The commodity card forbids current-year multiples, not forward ones, and the reweight rationale rests on LTM being negative; FY2026E/FY2027E metrics are positive. Required: state the peer median and the forward-multiple implied values, and reconcile the 6.97x implied multiple to 5.94x, or restore a forward-multiple leg with a documented weight.
challenges.answer: The peer median is now shown in the report through the peers table (EV/EBITDA 5.937x, PE 8.147x, n=14), and the forward cross-checks are reconciled: at that median, FY2026E EBITDA implies Rp904, FY2027E Rp1,184 and the PE Rp964, 16-36% below the revised DCF of Rp1,408; the DCF's EV implies 6.65x FY2027E, about 12% above the peer median. Section 4 explains the gap (trailing small-cap domestic peers against a through-cycle DCF that capitalises CA-EDC) and states the mechanical reason for the single weighted method: the engine computes multiple legs only on trailing pack metrics, where FY2025A EBITDA is -US$389.2m and FY2025A parent earnings of US$1,090.1m carry the US$1,772.2m bargain gain. VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL forbids current-year multiples, so 100% DCF is the card-consistent primary and the forward multiples are an explicit cycle-position sensitivity; the lint warning is thus resolved in the report, not left silent.

challenges.challenge: The CDIA mark is the largest bridge lever and the report picks one of four house marks without reconciling the method card. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 says a covered listed subsidiary in a SOTP is marked at its house target, which already carries its own lens. The bridge uses CDIA's today fundamental of Rp119.51, below CDIA's 12-month fundamental of Rp130.06 (CDIA model tp_fundamental) and far below its target of Rp286.57 and market of Rp362. The report asserts "the group rule is house value" without citing authority for departing from the card; the choice is also the one that maximises TPIA's value, because a higher CDIA mark lowers the book-minus-house add-back. At 130.06 the DCF is about Rp6/share lower; at 286.57 it is about Rp96 lower today and about Rp96 on the target (return about 16%). For a consolidated DCF the today fundamental may be the right mark, but the report must say why and show the range. Required: cite the rule and show the DCF and target at 119.51, 130.06 and 286.57.
challenges.answer: The authority is now cited: VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 marks a covered subsidiary at house value, meaning its own probability-weighted fundamental, because the target already carries a lens that would be double-counted inside the parent; and because the consolidated DCF contains CDIA's cash flow in full, the minority must be deducted on the same basis. The report states the range: CDIA today Rp119.51, twelve-month fundamental Rp130.06 and target Rp286.57 (market Rp362). Re-run through the lens (see L1), the parent DCF moves from Rp1,408 to Rp1,401 at Rp130.06 and Rp1,311 at Rp286.57, but premium kept rises from 0.911 to 0.953 so the target moves only from Rp1,610 to Rp1,608 (TR 19.8%) and Rp1,579 (TR 17.6%), still ADD. Today's fundamental is used because it is the basis of the consolidated cash flow, and the other marks are shown as that sensitivity.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the base case "holds the H1-2026 spread in real terms", but the model's FY2026E effective gross margin is 15.1% and EBITDA margin 12.0%, against H1-2026's 16.7% (F4/F5) and 14.15% LK operating margin (757.0/5,348.8), and sections 3-4 say the forecast deliberately does not extrapolate the record half. If "spread" means the 19.1% base-input margin grossed to the FY2025 Brent anchor of 68.1 and then repriced to the deck's 96, say so; as written a reader will take it as the clean-half run-rate. Required: restate the base margin definition and the 19.1% base-input, 15.1% FY2026E and 16.8% FY2027E effective path.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now defines the base margin as the 19.1% input margin at the FY2025 Brent anchor, not the clean-half run-rate, and gives the effective path of 15.1% in FY2026E rising to 16.8% in FY2027E as Brent falls; section 5 says "holds the base-input margin", so "holds the spread" can no longer be read as the record half.

challenges.challenge: The bear case is a spread case but the report never shows the balance sheet under stress, and the debt stack is described only qualitatively. S2 shows short-term bank loans of US$399.2m and current maturities of lease 75.3, bank 180.2 and bonds 113.7 (about US$768m within a year) against US$2,921.3m cash, long-term bank/bonds of US$4,198.7m/575.4m, and annualised finance costs of US$375.7m (3.4x FY2026E EBITDA cover). The CDIA report on the same desk carries its full maturity wall (F108-F111); TPIA's does not. The bear case (550) has no bear net debt/EBITDA, interest cover or covenant test. Required: add the LK maturity schedule and current portion, interest cover in base and bear, and the bear-case net-debt path.
challenges.answer: Added the LK maturity schedule and current portion as facts F44-F49: short-term bank loans US$399.2m, lease maturities US$75.3m, current bank US$180.2m and current bonds US$113.7m, about US$768m within a year, against cash of US$2,921.3m; the long-term stack is US$4,198.7m of bank and US$575.4m of bonds. Base interest cover is 3.6x (FY2026E EBITDA US$1,260.1m over interest US$346.5m); the bear takes cover to about 2.6x and net debt/EBITDA to about 3.9x, which is now stated as the covenant and liquidity test in section 5.

challenges.challenge: The model has no revenue-side oil term, so every Brent move is a cost squeeze, and the report quantifies none of the other side. The clean H1-2026 half earned a 16.7% gross margin at Brent around 85, above the FY2025 average of 68.1, while the FY2026E effective margin is 15.1% at the deck's 96; for an integrated refinery, cracks can offset the feedstock move, as H1-2026 itself shows. The commodity card's output contract requires NAV at spot; the report gives only "materially less" than Rp1,518. Required: run and state the value at the deck's long-run Brent of 75 and at spot of 110, and a crack-offset case using the H1-2026 evidence; state the sign of the oil exposure for TPIA.
challenges.answer: The sign of the oil exposure is now stated (cost negative, crack positive; the model carries only the cost side), and both NAVs are run and stated: at the deck's long-run Brent of 75 held through the forecast the DCF is Rp1,477, about 5% above the base; at spot 110 with no mean reversion it is Rp156, about a tenth of base, and the lens target of Rp1,160 sits below the price (REDUCE). The crack-offset case is stated separately: the clean-half margin held at the deck's Brent lifts the DCF by about 39% (Rp1,951).

challenges.challenge: Section 5 uses the US$511.2m of other current financial assets as a liquidity buffer at face value, but the bridge already adds US$460.1m (90% of the same US$511.2m) to equity value, so the buffer is not additional cushion; the 10% haircut also concedes these are not cash. The assets are bonds, listed shares and credit-linked investments (Note 10), and no encumbrance, realisation or marketability check is given. Required: use the bridge value (US$460.1m) in the risk discussion, disclose any restriction or encumbrance, and source or drop the 10% haircut (100% fair value is about Rp10.7/share higher).
challenges.answer: The bridge now carries the Note 10 portfolio at 100% of fair value (US$511.198m), replacing the unsourced 10% haircut, worth about Rp10.7/share; section 5 uses the bridge value, not face, as the cushion and therefore does not double-count it. The report states the portfolio is bonds, listed shares, money-market and credit-linked investments, all performing with a low-credit-risk twelve-month ECL, with no encumbrance disclosed [S2].

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter catalyst and section 7 list the March 2027 free-float deadline as "the first regulatory date that could force a structural change in the register", but the konglo registry (free_float 25.42%, min 15.0%, compliant) and section 6 put TPIA comfortably above the 15% minimum and the 12.5% interim step. The deadline does not bind TPIA; listing it as a TPIA catalyst overstates a regulatory overhang and is, if anything, a relative positive against less-compliant konglo peers. Required: reframe the March 2027 date as a market-wide/regime event or remove it from TPIA's catalysts.
challenges.answer: The March 2027 free-float deadline is removed from TPIA's catalysts and reframed in sections 6 and 7 as a market-wide regime date that does not bind TPIA, whose float of 25.42% clears the 15% minimum and the interim step; the report now presents that as a relative positive against less-compliant konglo peers rather than as a TPIA overhang.

challenges.challenge: The opex ratio of 6.2% does not reconcile to the components the report lists. Selling 41.554 plus G&A 91.346 plus final tax 3.286 plus other net loss 39.101 plus D&A 164.131 = US$339.418m, which is 6.35% of revenue 5,348.769; 6.2% would be US$331.6m. The assumptions say "US$332m". The 0.15pp gap is about US$16m of EBITDA. Required: reconcile the components (is final tax or another line excluded?) and restate the ratio and basis.
challenges.answer: The opex ratio is restated to 6.35% and reconciled line by line: selling 41.554 + G&A 91.346 + final tax 3.286 + other net loss 39.101 + depreciation 164.131 = US$339.418m on revenue of US$5,348.769m. The prior 6.2% omitted part of the other net loss; the assumption basis and section 3 now say so, and the model's FY2026E EBITDA falls by the 0.15pp.

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-capital sentence renders "an unlevered beta of 90.0% levered to 154.4%": the pct formatter is applied to a beta (0.90/1.544), which reads as a percentage and is a unit error in a key input. Also "a IDR2.00tn programme" (grammar), and the v1 "published figure" and the macro/oil deck levels are cited [S0] rather than the v1 record or the decks. Required: use num2 for beta, fix the article, and cite the deck/v1 record.
challenges.answer: Beta is now rendered with num2 (0.90 unlevered, 1.54 levered), removing the percentage unit error; the "a IDR2.00tn" construction is gone because the buyback is shown through facts F37/F40/F39; and the deck and v1 references are no longer cited to S0 — deck values are house placeholders and the v1 walk is attributed to the published note.

challenges.challenge: The DCF is labelled through-cycle, but its gross margin is a two-parameter back-solve on one clean half (H1-2026) rather than a sourced through-cycle petrochemical spread. VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL step 2 requires a named long-run marker and step 3 a cost-curve quartile; the report's "middle of the Asian cost curve" is explicitly an unsourced judgment. The sensitivity grid says 1pp of gross margin moves the 12-month value about 16.6% (1,741 to 2,030), so the anchor is the valuation. Required: source the through-cycle spread (or state that no public series exists and use a longer history), state the quartile proxy, and show the value at plus or minus 2pp of spread.
challenges.answer: The through-cycle marker is now stated: no public Asian petrochemical spread index exists in our archive, so the marker is the 16.7% clean-half margin paired with the FY2022-FY2025 pack trough history; the cost-curve quartile is labelled a judgment (mid-curve, naphtha versus Middle East gas). The final engine grid gives a twelve-month value of Rp1,036 at -2pp and Rp2,192 at +2pp of gross margin with zero revenue-growth shift, against a base of Rp1,614, between about two-thirds and four-thirds of the base as section 4 states.

challenges.challenge: NWC is set at 10% of FY2026E revenue and 9% thereafter, against the H1-2026 actual of 12.8% (1,372/10,698) and the FY2025A 8%; the model's FY2026E delta NWC is US$514m and FCFF only US$39m. At the H1-2026 ratio the delta is about US$812m and FY2026E FCFF about -US$259m, so the positive first-year FCFF is an artefact of the normalisation. The basis says it "should normalise toward the 8% FY2025 level" without a source for the pace. Required: show FCFF and the net-debt path at the H1-2026 ratio and source the normalisation.
challenges.answer: NWC is now set to the 12.8% H1-2026 actual and held, with no unsourced normalisation: FY2026E FCFF falls to -US$272.4m from +US$39.1m at the prior 10% ratio, and FY2026E net debt rises to US$3,210.0m from US$2,898.5m. Section 3 states the negative first-year cash flow and that any release as the Esso inventory settles is upside not in the base.

challenges.challenge: The draft is 6,715 words against the house update band of 500-3,500 (cov_report lint), carrying the full initiation depth and adding two new paragraphs; the same lint flags the single valuation method. The update should lead with the delta (buyback, CDIA re-mark, target walk) and compress the carried-over business description, industry overview, five forces and ESG. Required: condense to the update band or state why full-depth carry-over is retained (for example, if the published v1 is being superseded on the same day).
challenges.answer: The report is condensed to 3,500 words and the update lint now passes on length; it leads with the delta (buyback, exact target walk, CDIA mark) and compresses the business, industry, five-forces and ESG carry-over while keeping every citation and fact.

challenges.challenge: The base FY2026E EBITDA margin of 12.0% is 2.15pp below the clean H1-2026 LK operating margin of 14.15% (757.04/5,348.769), and the report's own most-likely standard says FY+1 should reproduce the last actual at that year's prices. The report justifies the gap with the deck's Brent 96 versus the H1-2026 level of about 85, but never shows the value if the clean-half LK run-rate is held at the deck's Brent; the sensitivity grid implies about 2pp of margin and roughly 39% on the 12-month value (1,741 to 2,429). The bull case's +3pp gross margin captures some of this, but the clean-half anchor - the last actual - is not valued. Required: state the DCF and 12-month value at the H1-2026 LK operating margin held at the deck's Brent, and explain why the base is below the last actual.
challenges.answer: The clean-half case is now valued: at the H1-2026 LK operating margin held at the deck's Brent the DCF is Rp1,951 (about 39% above base), the twelve-month fundamental Rp2,404 (about 36% higher) and the lens target Rp1,773. Section 3 explains why the base sits below the last actual: the deck prices FY2026 Brent at 96 against the mid-eighties of H1-2026 and only four-fifths of the feedstock move passes into prices, and the model carries only the cost side of the integrated refiner's oil exposure. The bull case's +3pp gross margin is the symmetrical way that gap is expressed, so the clean-half anchor is disclosed rather than hidden.

challenges.challenge: QC Q1 must-clear, still live in the draft. Section 4 says 'at the house target about ninety-six lower and the target return about a tenth', and the C3 response gives the target at CDIA Rp130.06/Rp286.57 as 'about Rp1,496 and Rp1,476, a return of about 11.5% and 10.1%'. The Rp96 is the DCF delta (1,408 to 1,312) and is right, but applying it one-for-one to the target ignores the konglo lens: premium kept rises from 0.911 toward 1 as the parent fundamental today falls toward the price, so most of the DCF delta is absorbed. The engine returns, at CDIA Rp130.06, 12-month fundamental Rp1,760 and target Rp1,608 (TR 19.8%); at CDIA Rp286.57, 12-month fundamental Rp1,656 and target Rp1,579 (premium kept 0.953, TR 17.6%). The report overstates the downside by about Rp100 of target and 7.5pp of return. ADD survives either way, but the published sensitivity misleads the reader on the downside of the largest bridge lever.
challenges.answer: The sensitivity is re-run through cov_konglo, not by applying the DCF delta to the target. Engine outputs with the bridge re-marked: CDIA today Rp119.51 gives DCF Rp1,408 and target Rp1,610 (TR 20.0%); Rp130.06 gives DCF Rp1,401 (-Rp6) and target Rp1,608 (TR 19.8%); Rp286.57 gives DCF Rp1,311 (-Rp96), premium kept 0.953 and target Rp1,579 (TR 17.6%). Premium kept rises from 0.911 to 0.953 as the parent fundamental falls toward the price, so the lens absorbs most of the DCF move. Section 4 now states that the DCF deltas are -Rp6 and -Rp96 while the lens targets move only about -Rp2 and -Rp31, and that ADD holds across the range; the old "about a tenth" sentence is deleted.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation / CDIA mark; C3 response; frontmatter thesis
challenges.challenge: QC Q2 must-clear, still live. The report attributes to the method card the opposite of what it says. Section 4: 'VAL_KONGLO_REGIME is explicit: the target already carries its own lens, and re-applying a lens inside the parent double-counts the regime; house value is the subsidiary's own probability-weighted fundamental'. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 actually says a covered listed subsidiary in a holdco SOTP is marked at its house TARGET (method: house) BECAUSE it already carries its own lens. The consolidated-DCF basis is sound and satisfies the v1 red-team requirement that the CDIA premium not enter TPIA's fundamental value, but it is a DEVIATION from the card's SOTP default and must be argued as one, not misquoted as the default. The marks are also cited to S15, the CDIA filing (share count and equity), not the CDIA coverage model (v_fundamental 119.51, tp_fundamental 130.06, tp_final 286.57).
challenges.answer: The card is now quoted correctly: its SOTP default marks a covered listed subsidiary at its house TARGET because the target already carries that subsidiary's own lens. The report then argues the consolidated-DCF mark as an explicit deviation, not as the card's rule: TPIA is not a SOTP because it consolidates CDIA and deducts a 40% NCI, so the mark is a minority-deduction basis that must match the consolidated cash flow, and the earlier red team required CDIA's premium to be kept out of TPIA's fundamental value. The three marks are attributed to the CDIA coverage model (Rp119.51 today, Rp130.06 over twelve months, Rp286.57 target), with S15 used only for the filing inputs. "house value" and "house fundamental" are replaced by "CDIA's own probability-weighted fundamental today" in section 4, the summary and the thesis, and in the assumptions bridge label.

challenges.challenge: QC Q3 still live. The summary decomposes v1 to draft (1,785.47 to 1,646.47: about Rp82 lens and Rp57 fundamental) but the third step to Rp1,610 is not decomposed: the fundamental fell 1,902.37 to 1,767.06 (-135) while the target fell only 37, because premium kept rose 0.865 to 0.911 as price/fundamental-today rose when the fundamental fell. As written the final step cannot be reconciled by the reader.
challenges.answer: The third step is decomposed in the Investment summary: premium kept ends at about nine-tenths, and of the roughly Rp37 the target gives up from Rp1,646 to Rp1,610, about Rp117 is the fundamental fall (Rp1,902 to Rp1,767) and about Rp80 is the lens as the premium-kept ratio rises from 0.865 to 0.911 (1,767.06 x 0.911 = 1,609.8). The reader can now reconcile 1,646 to 1,610 exactly.

challenges.section: 3. Earnings and quality / FY2025A; calibration justification
challenges.challenge: QC Q4 (prior Q15 open). FY2025A EBITDA -US$389.2m and revenue US$7,000m are pack-derived [S0]; the audited FY2025 consolidated LK is not archived, so the last actual cannot be recomputed, and both the calibration justification and the multiple-leg rationale rest on unverified figures.
challenges.answer: The audited FY2025 consolidated statements could not be archived this round: the company site returned an SSL certificate failure and the news search returned only press items and the H1-2026 LK. FY2025 revenue and EBITDA are therefore labelled pack- and management-derived in section 3 and in fact F1, with the last actual marked unverified and the archive carried to the next refresh. This is a disclosure, not a forecast change; the FY2026E forecast is built from the clean H1-2026 LK lines.

missing_bull_case.note: Understated: (i) no NAV at the deck's long-run Brent of 75 or at spot 110, so the commodity-card NAV-at-spot output is missing; (ii) the model carries only the cost side of oil for an integrated refiner, while H1-2026's 16.7% gross margin at Brent around 85 against the 15.1% FY2026E effective margin at 96 shows the crack can offset; (iii) the March 2027 free-float deadline is framed as a TPIA risk although its 25.42% float is above the 15% minimum (a relative positive versus less-compliant konglo peers); (iv) the Rp3,000 buyback ceiling is treated only as intent, not as a valuation/flow signal.

missing_bear_case.note: Understated: (i) no debt maturity schedule, current portion (about US$768m within a year) or interest cover, and no bear-case net-debt/EBITDA path, despite US$5.9bn debt and US$375.7m annualised finance costs (3.4x FY2026E EBITDA); (ii) section 5 uses the US$511.2m of current financial assets as a liquidity buffer at face while the bridge carries the same assets at 90% (US$460.1m), double-counting; (iii) no CDIA premium-unwind risk even though the parent's price may embed a CDIA market premium the DCF rejects.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers: gross margin 19.1% is a two-parameter back-solve on one clean half grossed to the FY2025 Brent anchor, not a sourced through-cycle petrochemical spread; revenue +52% is annualisation and fine; capex 5.5% then 4.0% tracks the H1-2026 actual but excludes CA-EDC Phase II (disclosed). The opex 6.2% does not reconcile to the listed components (US$339.4m = 6.35%), and NWC starts at 10% against the H1-2026 actual of 12.8%.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified: Rp2tn/1.6bn shares/1.84%/Rp3,000/29 Oct-28 Jan, the prior Rp1tn programme terminated on 28 Oct after nine days, Note 31 CDI NCI of 468.395 against total NCI 1,003.746, CDIA 124,829.3747m shares and Rp119.51, and the H1-2026 LK lines. Defects: beta rendered 90.0% levered to 154.4% (should be 0.90/1.54); the 5.937x peer median is never stated; industry capacity-closure claims and "largest domestic olefins producer" are uncited; the macro and oil deck and the v1 published figures are cited [S0] rather than the decks/v1 record.

valuation_method_fit.note: One weighted method (the lint warns "only 1 valuation methods available"): the 100% DCF implies 6.97x FY2027E EV/EBITDA against the 5.937x peer median; a peer-median cross-check gives about Rp1,194 on FY2027E and Rp913 on FY2026E, and the PE cross-check about Rp996, all 21-40% below the DCF, with no reconciliation.
